title: Medical Evidence: Summons, Subpoena and Dying Declaration

steps.title: The statutory nature of summons and subpoena
steps.tx: In judicial procedure, a formal **court witness summons order** constitutes a solemn legal mandate issued by a judicial officer compelling the appearance of a designated person at a specified date and time to give evidence or produce documents. Delivered through a police officer or registered postal service, willful disobedience of a court summons without valid legal excuse constitutes contempt of court, risking arrest under bailable or non-bailable warrants.
steps.say: A court summons is a legal command to attend court and testify on a specified date. Disobeying summons without valid excuse risks contempt and arrest warrants.

rows: Signed by presiding judge with court seal

steps.tx: The paper that compels a doctor to attend is a **witness summons**. Under the old Code it was Section 61. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita the corresponding order is Section 63. It names the person, the court, the day and the purpose, evidence or documents, and it carries the court seal. Service is by a police officer or by registered post. Ignoring it without a lawful excuse is contempt, and a warrant can follow.
steps.say: A summons under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, the successor of Section 61 of the old Code, orders a named witness to attend. The court seal is on it. Disobedience without excuse is contempt.

steps.title: Subpoena duces tecum and document production
steps.tx: When medical evidence requires written records, courts issue a specialized **subpoena duces tecum writ**, ordering the medical superintendent or treating clinician to appear carrying specific original patient charts, surgical logs, radiological films, or medicolegal registers. The clinician must produce the original handwritten records in court, where certified true copies are submitted for the official judicial file while originals are verified by counsel.
steps.say: A subpoena duces tecum orders the hospital or clinician to produce original treatment charts, postmortem registers, and X-rays in court for judicial verification.

steps.title: Priority rules when receiving conflicting summons
steps.tx: When a busy clinician receives simultaneous court summonses scheduled for the identical calendar date, well-established **summons priority operational rules** govern attendance decisions. Criminal court summonses take absolute precedence over civil court summonses. Between courts of unequal status, the higher-ranking court takes precedence over a lower bench. Between courts of equal rank, the summons received earlier in chronological order dictates attendance.
steps.say: When summons dates clash, criminal courts take priority over civil courts, higher courts take priority over lower ones, and earlier received summonses take priority among equals.

steps.title: Definition and philosophy of dying declarations
steps.tx: Originating from the Latin maxim nemo moriturus praesumitur mentiri, the **dying declaration evidentiary principle** holds that a dying individual is presumed incapable of falsehood on the threshold of death. Under Indian law, a dying declaration represents a statement made by a person regarding the cause of their death or the circumstances of the transaction resulting in their fatal condition, admissible as primary legal evidence.
steps.say: A dying declaration is a statement by a dying victim regarding the circumstances of their death, accepted as evidence because a person facing death is presumed truthful.

steps.title: Comparison between Indian and English law on dying declarations
steps.tx: A critical medicolegal distinction exists regarding the **expectation of death requirement** between British and Indian jurisprudence. Under English common law, the declarant must possess an absolute settled hopeless expectation of imminent death for the declaration to be admissible. Conversely, under Indian law, actual expectation of impending death is not essential; the statement remains fully admissible even if the declarant had hopes of recovery.
steps.say: Under English law, the patient must have an absolute expectation of imminent death. Under Indian law, expectation of death is not required for the statement to be admissible.

left.title: Indian law (Section 26 BSA)
points: Expectation of death is not mandatory
Can be recorded by magistrate, doctor or police

right.title: English common law
points: Settled hopeless expectation of death required
Strict religious presumption of final truth

steps.title: Who may record a dying declaration
steps.tx: While an Executive or Judicial Magistrate represents the **preferred dying declaration recorder**, statutory law recognizes statements recorded by treating physicians, police officers, village headmen, or even private citizens when death is rapidly approaching. However, declarations recorded by magistrates carry the highest probative value in trial courts, while police-recorded statements are viewed with strict judicial caution due to risks of coaching or duress.
steps.say: Magistrates are preferred to record dying declarations. If time is short, treating doctors or police officers may record the statement to prevent evidence loss.

steps.title: The crucial role of the medical officer during recording
steps.tx: During the recording process, the **compos mentis medical certification** represents the most vital legal safeguard protecting the integrity of the declaration. The treating doctor must personally examine the patient and endorse on the paper that the victim was conscious, coherent, and mentally competent before recording commences, throughout the questioning, and at the conclusion of the statement.
steps.say: The doctor must certify in writing that the patient is conscious and mentally sound before, during, and after recording the dying declaration.

steps.tx: Before a dying declaration is taken, the treating doctor examines the patient and writes that consciousness, coherence, and mental competence were present. That endorsement is the **compos mentis medical certification**, the safeguard that protects the statement's legal integrity. The same fitness must be confirmed before questioning starts, while questions continue, and again when the statement ends, so later readers can see the victim remained competent throughout.

steps.title: Standard protocol and format for recording statements
steps.tx: The formal **question and answer protocol** must follow strict evidentiary conventions to avoid judicial rejection during trial. The recorder must exclude all investigating police personnel and relatives from the room to eliminate coaching. The statement is documented in the patient's own vernacular words without prompting, read back to the patient, affirmed, and endorsed with the declarant's signature or left thumbprint.
steps.say: The statement is written in question-and-answer format using the patient's own words. Relatives and police are sent outside, and the text is read back before signing.

rows: Demonstrates lack of leading or suggestive questions
Establishes authentic execution by the victim

steps.title: Evidentiary outcome if the declarant survives
steps.tx: When a gravely wounded victim unexpectedly recovers after providing a statement, the **surviving declarant legal transformation** dictates that the document completely ceases to be a dying declaration under Section 26 BSA. Instead, the written statement transforms into a prior recorded statement, which can only be utilized in court under Section 157 BSA to corroborate or contradict the victim's live testimony from the witness box.
steps.say: If the injured patient survives, the dying declaration loses its special status and becomes an ordinary prior statement used to support or challenge their testimony.
